doc.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Big band drumming with Louie Bellson and Mel Lewis
summary: Shaughnessy says he, Bellson and Mel Lewis shaped modern big band drumming and that you must move with the times while keeping your own identity.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Right. You and Louie Bellson and a few other guys have just kind of defined modern jazz big band drumming I think. Would you agree with that?

Yes, I think we’ve had some influence in it. I think another fine contributor, and I’m sure you would agree would be the late Mel Lewis, a wonderful drummer in his manner and style of playing. Yeah. But I think that Louie and myself both kind of have tried to move with the times because you can’t really play big band quite the same today as you would have played it thirty years ago, you know, not quite. And I think we’ve both tried to move with the times and I think still try to retain your own identity. That’s the secret. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
